claims.text: Wear performance of high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by formation of a stable, single-phase solid solution with high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy decreases the Gibbs free energy of the solid solution.
The decrease in Gibbs free energy stabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
A stable single-phase solid solution improves coating hardness.
A stable single-phase solid solution improves strength.
A stable single-phase solid solution improves wear resistance.
A stable single-phase solid solution improves corrosion resistance.
Configurational entropy, lattice distortion, and sluggish diffusion are structural mediators of wear performance.
In-situ TEM or AFM can reveal wear-induced microstructural changes relevant to the proposed mechanism.
The high-entropy-alloy coatings will have greater hardness than conventional alloys.
The high-entropy-alloy coatings will have enhanced corrosion resistance relative to conventional alloys.
The high-entropy-alloy coatings will exhibit a 20–30% increase in wear resistance relative to conventional alloys.
Single-phase high-entropy-alloy coatings remain stable under high-temperature and high-pressure wear conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant 20–30% reduction in wear rate relative to a conventional-alloy control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is already defined as a single-phase solid solution, whereas the mechanism is framed as formation of that phase; no intervention is specified that changes or induces phase formation.
